tranche: Q5 new source families (audio DSP review, hosted-bot talents, patent prompts, building-energy multi-agent, Japanese novel/manga workspace, Unity editor CLI)
source_role: original-author source discovered in GitSkills G2 (dynamic discovery; not a registered source)
review_kind: exact-pinned 10-dimension static source-vetting candidate decisions (not governed review)
review_method: Parallel read-only reviewers on disjoint exact package lists with one shared brief (see docs/reviews/2026-11-03-q5-six-new-source-families-static.md); package files read at the pin except where coverage says otherwise; SKILL.md matched case-insensitively; integration owner validated identity against git ls-tree, taxonomy, score/rationale agreement and hard-fail/disposition consistency, applied the 10/20 floor, and applied family harmonizations by independent adjudicators (openclaw, patent prompts, monogatari). Nothing executed, installed or fetched from candidates.
macro_findings: 15 US patent drafting/prosecution prompt skills; each SKILL.md is a thin shim that loads ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../../<area>/prompt.md outside the package (present at the pin; works only with the whole plugin layout). Pure text generation; nothing files or posts.

prior-art-analysis directs web searches on unpublished pre-filing claims without asking first (private-data-egress; REJECT). Searches of an accused or competitor product are exempt under the family rule.
No not-legal-advice caveat in the prompts the host runs (README only); SKILL.md inputs often do not match prompt placeholders; ambiguous '---' prompt delimiters can truncate instructions.

Legal gaps: 112(f) limited to a closed term list; prior-art prompt omits AIA 102(b)(1) exceptions and secondary considerations; 101 prompt lacks the Alice/Mayo two-step; continuation skills omit copendency under 35 U.S.C. 120 and double patenting; induced-infringement analysis omits knowledge/intent.
